developments.why_it_matters: Distribution, regulatory licenses, clearing, market making and event-data quality are becoming a new financial-market stack. Volume alone does not prove durable economics.

developments.summary: CFTC industry filings show multiple new or pending designated contract markets in June and July 2026, expanding the regulated venue layer for event contracts and adjacent products.
developments.title: CFTC DCM designations broaden prediction-market and event-contract infrastructure
developments.why_it_matters: The chokepoints may shift toward licensing, clearing, market surveillance, liquidity distribution and brokerage access. A new venue designation is not proof of product-market fit or token value capture.

developments.summary: Coinbase reported that Marex is accepting USDC as collateral in regulated derivatives clearing with conversion and reporting infrastructure supplied by Coinbase.
developments.title: USDC enters regulated derivatives-margin workflow through Coinbase and Marex
developments.why_it_matters: Stablecoins are moving from exchange settlement into regulated collateral workflows. War Room must track collateral eligibility, haircuts, clearing-member adoption, custody and issuer/platform fee capture.

developments.summary: Circle announced final OCC approval to establish a national trust bank focused initially on federally supervised digital-asset custody, with reserve-management capability contemplated later.
developments.title: Circle receives final OCC approval for a national trust bank
developments.why_it_matters: Stablecoin competition is shifting from token issuance toward regulated custody, reserve infrastructure, clearing and institutional distribution. The investment question is fee capture, reserve economics and adoption—not a generic bullish stablecoin label.

developments.summary: The Ethereum Foundation described coordinated AI agents testing protocol code and emphasized that triage and reproducible proof—not candidate count—determine whether a finding is real.
developments.title: Ethereum protocol-security team reports agent-assisted discovery and triage of real bugs
developments.why_it_matters: As agentic trading and autonomous onchain execution expand, security triage, reproducibility and permission controls become bottlenecks. Agent output is evidence inventory, not an oracle or automatic exploit-risk score.

developments.summary: Robinhood launched the public mainnet of its Arbitrum-based Layer 2, with Stock Tokens, DEX integrations, lending primitives and an explicit real-world-asset focus.
developments.title: Robinhood Chain public mainnet and onchain distribution
developments.why_it_matters: Distribution, tokenization, settlement, collateral and DeFi may converge inside a retail brokerage ecosystem. The investment question is who captures fees, liquidity and developer mindshare rather than merely who announces a chain.

developments.summary: Robinhood made Stock Tokens available through its wallet in many jurisdictions, enabling 24/7 trading and potential use in lending pools and as collateral, subject to jurisdictional restrictions.
developments.title: Stock Tokens become transferable DeFi assets
developments.why_it_matters: This changes the competitive map from tokenized price exposure to composable financial collateral. Legal form, redemption, issuer credit risk, liquidity fragmentation and underlying-share rights remain critical.

developments.summary: Robinhood announced onchain USDG lending through Morpho-based infrastructure and plans for AI-connected crypto trading accounts using its Trading MCP.
developments.title: Onchain lending and agentic crypto accounts enter retail distribution
developments.why_it_matters: The key shift is brokerage distribution of self-custody lending and automated execution. This creates new growth surfaces but also smart-contract, model, execution, monitoring and suitability risks.

developments.summary: The SEC issued a Commission-level interpretation clarifying the application of federal securities laws to certain crypto assets and transactions, with related CFTC guidance.
developments.title: SEC/CFTC crypto-asset interpretation changes the regulatory map
developments.why_it_matters: Regulatory classification changes access, listing, custody, token design and capital formation. War Room must track asset-by-asset legal status rather than use a generic regulatory score.

doctrine: Start from an important decision problem, not an available dataset.
Detect what has already changed before forecasting what may change.
Study historical winners and losers; explain mechanisms, not resemblance.
Record contradictory evidence and uncertainty explicitly.
Explain the rational counterparty and the source of advantage.
Run the cheapest valid falsifier against a strong market-specific baseline.
Ablate complexity and inspect failure piles, not only aggregate metrics.
No prospective evidence means no capital permission.
Fresh official-source changes require human review and never become automatic directional claims.
FX is pair-specific; a price-only state can never become a triggered watch.
Options and Greek modules appear only where product and data capability gates pass.
Generic OHLCV screens are context screens, never directional selectors.
No scenario headroom, probability or EV without point-in-time economic inputs and calibrated probabilities.
